question: Two numbers are respectively 30% and 18% more than a third number. The ratio of the two numbers is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **third number** is 100.

First number = 100 + 30% of 100 = 130.

Second number = 100 + 18% of 100 = 118.

Ratio = 130 : 118 = 65 : 59.

**∴ The correct answer is 65 : 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First number is 30% more than the third. Second number is 18% more than the third.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf5890a9fcc82bd47a830645f69776bd44acc133a43d06caaee58c1d942fddd5.png] 

Let the **third number** be x.

⇒ First number = x + 0.30x = 1.30x

⇒ Second number = x + 0.18x = 1.18x

⇒ Ratio = First number ÷ Second number

⇒ Ratio = 1.30x ÷ 1.18x

⇒ Ratio = 130 / 118

⇒ Ratio = 65 / 59

**∴ The correct answer is 65 : 59.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Increase

If a value increases by r%, the new value is (1 + r/100) × Original Value.

Ratio Comparison

A ratio a : b can be expressed as a fraction a/b and simplified by dividing both terms by their HCF.

Base Value Selection

In percentage problems comparing multiple items to one common item, assume the common item (base) as 100 for easier calculation.</p
